reason: The text (Exodus 17:8-16) depicts the battle against Amalek and demonstrates Yahweh's active military support for Israel. Moses holds up God's staff, and Israel prevails when his hands are raised, showing divine loyalty and intervention on behalf of the people. The passage concludes with God's commitment to completely erase the memory of Amalek ('I will completely wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens'), reinforcing divine support for Israel. There is no textual indication that Yahweh considers replacing Israel with another people, nor any suggestion that He refuses loyalty to them. The narrative explicitly demonstrates the opposite—active divine loyalty through military assistance.
